+  In the situation of \ref{lem:appTop_map_appLE}, for every \(r \in k\) the map
+  \(\pi^\sharp : \Gamma(Y, U) \to \Gamma(X, V)\) sends the image of \(r\) under the
+  structure algebra map of \(Y\) (Definition~\ref{def:overAlgebraMap}) to the image of
+  \(r\) under the structure algebra map of \(X\).
+\end{lemma}
+\begin{proof}
+  \leanok
+  Evaluate the equality of ring homomorphisms of \ref{lem:appTop_map_appLE} at the section
+  corresponding to \(r\).
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[The basic-open models lie over the base]
+  \label{lem:P1_awayi_structureMap}
+  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.P1.awayι_structureMap}
+  \uses{def:P1_structureMap}
+  \leanok
+  Let \(f \in k[X_0, X_1]\) be homogeneous of positive degree. The composite of the affine
+  model \(\Spec A_{(f)} \to \PP^1\) of the basic open \(D_+(f)\) with the structure
+  morphism \(\PP^1 \to \Spec k\) is the morphism induced by the algebra map
+  \(k \to A_{(f)}\). (This generalizes \ref{lem:P1_chartIota_structureMap} from the two
+  standard charts to all standard basic opens.)
+\end{lemma}
+\begin{proof}
+  \leanok
+  \uses{def:P1_gradeZero}
+  As for \ref{lem:P1_chartIota_structureMap}: the canonical morphism
+  \(\Proj A \to \Spec A_0\), restricted to the affine model of a basic open, is induced by
+  the ring homomorphism \(A_0 \to A_{(f)}\), and composing with the isomorphism
+  \(k \cong A_0\) of \ref{def:P1_gradeZero} gives the claim.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[The basic-open inclusion factors through its affine model]
+  \label{lem:P1_basicOpen_iota_eq}
+  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.P1.basicOpen_ι_eq}
+  \uses{def:P1}
+  \leanok
+  Let \(f \in k[X_0, X_1]\) be homogeneous of positive degree. The inclusion
+  \(D_+(f) \to \PP^1\) is the composite of the canonical identification
+  \(D_+(f) \cong \Spec A_{(f)}\) with the affine model \(\Spec A_{(f)} \to \PP^1\).
+\end{lemma}
+\begin{proof}
+  \leanok
+  The affine model is by construction an open immersion with image \(D_+(f)\), and the
+  canonical identification is the induced isomorphism onto the image; composing the two
+  recovers the inclusion.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[The structure algebra map on a basic open]
+  \label{lem:P1_structureMap_appTop_awayToSection}
+  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.P1.structureMap_appTop_awayToSection}
+  \uses{def:P1_structureMap, lem:P1_awayi_structureMap, lem:P1_basicOpen_iota_eq}
+  \leanok
+  Let \(f \in k[X_0, X_1]\) be homogeneous of positive degree. The composite
+  \[
+    \Gamma(\Spec k, \top) \to \Gamma(\PP^1, \top) \to \Gamma\bigl(\PP^1, D_+(f)\bigr)
+  \]
+  (structure morphism on global sections, then restriction) is the composite of the
+  identification \(\Gamma(\Spec k, \top) \cong k\), the algebra map \(k \to A_{(f)}\), and
+  the canonical map \(A_{(f)} \to \Gamma(\PP^1, D_+(f))\).
+\end{lemma}
+\begin{proof}
+  \leanok
+  By \ref{lem:P1_basicOpen_iota_eq} and \ref{lem:P1_awayi_structureMap}, the composite of
+  the inclusion \(D_+(f) \to \PP^1\) with the structure morphism is the identification
+  \(D_+(f) \cong \Spec A_{(f)}\) followed by the morphism induced by \(k \to A_{(f)}\).
+  Taking global sections of this equality of scheme morphisms, and identifying the global
+  sections of the open subscheme \(D_+(f)\) with \(\Gamma(\PP^1, D_+(f))\) --- under which
+  the map on sections induced by the identification with \(\Spec A_{(f)}\) becomes the
+  canonical map \(A_{(f)} \to \Gamma(\PP^1, D_+(f))\) --- yields the claim.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[The distinguished fraction of a chart pair is the chart coordinate]
+  \label{lem:P1_isLocalizationElem_X_eq}
+  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.P1.isLocalizationElem_X_eq}
+  \uses{def:P1_chartCoord}
+  \leanok
+  For \(i, j \in \{0,1\}\), the canonical degree-zero fraction
+  \(X_j^{\deg X_i} / X_i^{\deg X_j}\) attached to the pair \((X_i, X_j)\) of homogeneous
+  elements equals the chart coordinate \(t_{ij} = X_j / X_i \in A_{(X_i)}\).
+\end{lemma}
+\begin{proof}
+  \leanok
+  Both degrees are one, and a first power is the element itself.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{theorem}[The chart coordinate cuts out the overlap]
+  \label{thm:P1_basicOpen_chartCoord}
+  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.P1.basicOpen_awayToSection_chartCoord}
+  \uses{def:P1_chartOpen, def:P1_chartCoord, lem:P1_basicOpen_iota_eq,
+    lem:P1_isLocalizationElem_X_eq}
+  \leanok
+  For \(i, j \in \{0,1\}\), regard the chart coordinate \(t_{ij} \in A_{(X_i)}\) as a
+  section of the structure sheaf over the chart \(U_i = D_+(X_i)\), via the canonical map
+  \(A_{(X_i)} \to \Gamma(\PP^1, U_i)\). Then the basic open of this section in the scheme
+  \(\PP^1\) --- the locus of \(U_i\) where it is invertible --- is the chart overlap:
+  \[
+    D(t_{ij}) \;=\; U_i \cap U_j .
+  \]
+\end{theorem}
+\begin{proof}
+  \leanok
+  Both sides are open subsets of \(U_i\) (the basic open of a section over \(U_i\) is
+  contained in \(U_i\)), so it suffices to show that they have the same preimage under the
+  identification \(U_i \cong \Spec A_{(X_i)}\), and to transport the equality forward
+  along this open immersion. No stalks are involved: everything is transported through
+  the affine model.
+
+  On the one hand, the preimage of the basic open \(D(t_{ij})\) is the basic open of
+  \(\Spec A_{(X_i)}\) at the ring element \(t_{ij}\): under the identification of an
+  affine open with the spectrum of its section ring, scheme-level basic opens of sections
+  correspond to spectrum-level basic opens of ring elements.
+
+  On the other hand, the preimage of \(U_j = D_+(X_j)\) under the affine model
+  \(\Spec A_{(X_i)} \to \PP^1\) (through which the inclusion of \(U_i\) factors,
+  \ref{lem:P1_basicOpen_iota_eq}) is the basic open at the canonical degree-zero fraction
+  attached to the pair \((X_i, X_j)\): a homogeneous prime avoiding \(X_i\) avoids
+  \(X_j\) exactly when the degree-zero fraction \(X_j/X_i\) is invertible in the
+  corresponding localization. By \ref{lem:P1_isLocalizationElem_X_eq} this fraction is
+  \(t_{ij}\), so the preimage of \(U_i \cap U_j\) is again the basic open at
+  \(t_{ij}\).
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[The Laurent generators as restrictions from the charts]
+  \label{lem:P1_laurent_generators}
+  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.P1.overlapSectionsEquiv_symm_T,
+    AlgebraicGeometry.P1.overlapSectionsEquiv_symm_T_neg,
+    AlgebraicGeometry.P1.overlapSectionsEquiv_symm_algebraMap}
+  \uses{def:P1_overlapSectionsEquiv, def:P1_chartCoord}
+  \leanok
+  Under the identification
+  \(\gamma_{01} : \Gamma(\PP^1, U_0 \cap U_1) \cong k[T, T^{-1}]\) of
+  \ref{def:P1_overlapSectionsEquiv}:
+  \begin{enumerate}
+    \item \(T\) corresponds to the restriction to the overlap of the chart coordinate
+      \(t_{01}\), regarded as a section over \(U_0\);
+    \item \(T^{-1}\) corresponds to the restriction to the overlap of the chart
+      coordinate \(t_{10}\), regarded as a section over \(U_1\);
+    \item each scalar \(r \in k\) corresponds to the section over the overlap given by
+      the image of \(r\) under the algebra map \(k \to A_{(X_0X_1)}\).
+  \end{enumerate}
+\end{lemma}
+\begin{proof}
+  \leanok
+  \uses{lem:P1_res_left, lem:P1_res_right}
+  (1) and (2): by \ref{lem:P1_res_left} (resp.\ \ref{lem:P1_res_right}), restriction from
+  the chart \(U_0\) (resp.\ \(U_1\)) to the overlap corresponds, under the
+  identifications \(\gamma_0, \gamma_1, \gamma_{01}\), to \(t \mapsto T\) (resp.\
+  \(t \mapsto T^{-1}\)); apply this to the sections corresponding to the polynomial
+  \(t\), which are the chart coordinates. (3): \(\gamma_{01}\) is built from the
+  \(k\)-algebra isomorphism \(\theta\) of \ref{def:P1_overlapAlgEquiv}, hence matches the
+  two algebra maps from \(k\).
+\end{proof}
+
+\section{Finiteness of the first cohomology}
+
+Combining the two-affine-cover cokernel bridge with the two-lattice ladder of
+Chapter~\ref{chap:Algebra} along a finite morphism to the projective line yields the
+finiteness of \(H^1\). Classically this computation goes back to the explicit \v{C}ech
+computation of the cohomology of projective space --- for \(\PP^1\) itself, the
+description of \(H^1\) as the cokernel of the two-chart restriction-difference map into
+the Laurent ring, spanned by the finitely many ``negative'' monomials --- extended to a
+curve by pushing forward along a finite morphism; the two-lattice ladder is exactly the
+abstraction of that monomial bookkeeping.
+
+\begin{theorem}[Finiteness of \(H^1\) along a finite morphism to the projective line]
+  \label{thm:moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1}
+  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1}
+  \uses{def:HModule, def:moduleKSheaf, def:P1_structureMap}
+  \leanok
+  \source{hartshorne-algebraic-geometry:page-0242, hartshorne-algebraic-geometry:page-0243}
+  Let \(k\) be a field, \(X\) a scheme over \(\Spec k\), and \(\pi : X \to \PP^1\) a
+  finite morphism over \(k\) (its composite with the structure morphism of \(\PP^1\) is
+  the structure morphism of \(X\)). Then \(H^1\bigl(X, \struct{X/k}\bigr)\) is a finite
+  \(k\)-module.
+\end{theorem}
+\begin{proof}
+  \leanok
+  \uses{lem:preimage_chart_affine, lem:preimage_chart_sup, lem:finite_app_overlap,
+    lem:P1_chartOpen_inf, thm:TwoCover_h1CokEquiv, def:TwoCover_diff, def:TwoCover_H1Cok,
+    def:P1_overlapSectionsEquiv, def:P1_chartCoord, lem:P1_laurent_generators,
+    lem:appLE_overAlgebraMap, lem:P1_structureMap_appTop_awayToSection,
+    thm:P1_basicOpen_chartCoord, cor:two_lattice_loc_pow}
+  Write \(U_0, U_1\) for the standard charts of \(\PP^1\) and set
+  \(V_i = \pi^{-1}(U_i)\).
+
+  (a) \emph{The cover and the cokernel.} Since \(\pi\) is finite, hence affine, the
+  \(V_i\) are affine opens of \(X\) (\ref{lem:preimage_chart_affine}), and they cover
+  \(X\) (\ref{lem:preimage_chart_sup}). By the two-affine-cover bridge
+  \ref{thm:TwoCover_h1CokEquiv},
+  \[
+    H^1\bigl(X, \struct{X/k}\bigr) \;\cong\;
+      N \big/ \mathrm{range}(\mathrm{diff}),
+    \qquad N := \Gamma(X, V_0 \cap V_1),
+  \]
+  with \(\mathrm{diff}(s_0, s_1) = s_0|_{V_0 \cap V_1} - s_1|_{V_0 \cap V_1}\)
+  (\ref{def:TwoCover_diff}). It therefore suffices to prove that this quotient is a
+  finite \(k\)-module.
+
+  (b) \emph{The Laurent module structure.} Preimages commute with intersections, and
+  \(U_0 \cap U_1 = D_+(X_0X_1)\) (\ref{lem:P1_chartOpen_inf}), so
+  \(V_0 \cap V_1 = \pi^{-1}(U_0 \cap U_1)\). Make \(N\) an algebra over the Laurent
+  polynomial ring via the composite
+  \[
+    k[T, T^{-1}] \xrightarrow{\ \gamma_{01}^{-1}\ } \Gamma(\PP^1, U_0 \cap U_1)
+      \xrightarrow{\ \pi^\sharp\ } \Gamma\bigl(X, \pi^{-1}(U_0 \cap U_1)\bigr) = N
+  \]
+  (\ref{def:P1_overlapSectionsEquiv}). This structure is compatible with the \(k\)-module
+  structure of \(N\): a scalar \(r \in k[T,T^{-1}]\) corresponds under \(\gamma_{01}\) to
+  the image of \(r\) under the algebra map into the overlap ring
+  (\ref{lem:P1_laurent_generators}(3)), which is the structure algebra map of \(\PP^1\)
+  on \(U_0 \cap U_1\) (\ref{lem:P1_structureMap_appTop_awayToSection}), and \(\pi\) pulls
+  the structure algebra map of \(\PP^1\) back to that of \(X\)
+  (\ref{lem:appLE_overAlgebraMap}). Hence the \(k\)-module structure of \(N\) is the
+  restriction of scalars of the \(k[T,T^{-1}]\)-structure along the canonical map
+  \(k \to k[T,T^{-1}]\).
+
+  (c) \emph{Module-finiteness over the Laurent ring.} Since \(\pi\) is finite and
+  \(U_0 \cap U_1\) is an affine open of \(\PP^1\), the map
+  \(\pi^\sharp : \Gamma(\PP^1, U_0 \cap U_1) \to N\) is module-finite
+  (\ref{lem:finite_app_overlap}); composing with the isomorphism \(\gamma_{01}^{-1}\),
+  \(N\) is a finite \(k[T,T^{-1}]\)-module.
+
+  (d) \emph{The two lattices, and the range of the difference map.} Let
+  \(Q_0, Q_1 \subseteq N\) be the images of the (\(k\)-linear) restriction maps
+  \(\Gamma(X, V_0) \to N\) and \(\Gamma(X, V_1) \to N\). Then
+  \(\mathrm{range}(\mathrm{diff}) = Q_0 + Q_1\): every value
+  \(s_0| - s_1|\) of \(\mathrm{diff}\) is the sum of \(s_0| \in Q_0\) and
+  \(-(s_1|) = (-s_1)| \in Q_1\); conversely \(s_0| = \mathrm{diff}(s_0, 0) \) and
+  \(s_1| = \mathrm{diff}(0, -s_1)\) exhibit every element of \(Q_0\) and of \(Q_1\) as a
+  value of \(\mathrm{diff}\) --- the sign is absorbed because \(Q_1\) is the image of a
+  linear map.
+
+  (e) \emph{Lattice stability.} Let
+  \(\tau_0 = \pi^\sharp(t_{01}) \in \Gamma(X, V_0)\) and
+  \(\tau_1 = \pi^\sharp(t_{10}) \in \Gamma(X, V_1)\) be the pullbacks of the chart
+  coordinates, regarded as sections over the charts
+  (Definition~\ref{def:P1_chartCoord}). By \ref{lem:P1_laurent_generators}(1) and the
+  compatibility of \(\pi^\sharp\) with restriction, \(T\) acts on \(N\) as
+  multiplication by \(\tau_0|_{V_0 \cap V_1}\); symmetrically \(T^{-1}\) acts as
+  multiplication by \(\tau_1|_{V_0 \cap V_1}\) (\ref{lem:P1_laurent_generators}(2)).
+  Hence \(Q_0\) is stable under multiplication by \(T\): for \(s \in \Gamma(X, V_0)\),
+  \[
+    T \cdot s|_{V_0 \cap V_1} \;=\; \tau_0|\cdot s| \;=\; (\tau_0 s)|_{V_0 \cap V_1}
+      \;\in\; Q_0,
+  \]
+  and symmetrically \(Q_1\) is stable under multiplication by \(T^{-1}\).
+
+  (f) \emph{Absorption up to powers.} The overlap is a basic open inside each chart
+  preimage: pulling back the identity \(D(t_{ij}) = U_i \cap U_j\) of
+  \ref{thm:P1_basicOpen_chartCoord} along \(\pi\) (basic opens of sections pull back to
+  basic opens of the pulled-back sections) gives
+  \[
+    V_0 \cap V_1 = D(\tau_0) \subseteq V_0,
+    \qquad
+    V_0 \cap V_1 = D(\tau_1) \subseteq V_1 .
+  \]
+  Since \(V_0\) is affine and \(V_0 \cap V_1\) is its basic open defined by \(\tau_0\),
+  restriction identifies \(N\) with the localization of \(\Gamma(X, V_0)\) at the powers
+  of \(\tau_0\) (quasi-coherence of the structure sheaf). Hence for every \(n \in N\)
+  there are \(m \ge 0\) and \(a \in \Gamma(X, V_0)\) with
+  \(n \cdot (\tau_0|)^m = a|\), i.e.\ \(T^m \cdot n \in Q_0\). Symmetrically, every
+  \(n \in N\) satisfies \(T^{-m} \cdot n \in Q_1\) for some \(m \ge 0\).
+
+  (g) \emph{The ladder.} By (b), (c), (e) and (f), the module \(N\) over
+  \(k[T,T^{-1}]\) with the \(k\)-submodules \(Q_0, Q_1\) satisfies all hypotheses of the
+  two-lattice finiteness theorem in its localization form via powers of the generator
+  (\ref{cor:two_lattice_loc_pow}); hence \(N/(Q_0 + Q_1)\) is a finite \(k\)-module. By
+  (d) this quotient is \(N/\mathrm{range}(\mathrm{diff})\), and by (a) it is
+  \(H^1\bigl(X, \struct{X/k}\bigr)\).
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{theorem}[Finiteness of \(H^1\) of the curve]
+  \label{thm:moduleFinite_hModule_one}
+  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.moduleFinite_hModule_one}
+  \uses{def:HModule, def:moduleKSheaf}
+  \leanok
+  Let \(k\) be a field and \(C\) a smooth curve over \(k\) (proper, smooth of relative
+  dimension one, geometrically irreducible). Then
+  \(H^1\bigl(C, \struct{C/k}\bigr)\) is a finite \(k\)-module; equivalently, it is a
+  finite-dimensional \(k\)-vector space.
+\end{theorem}
+\begin{proof}
+  \leanok
+  \uses{thm:exists_finite_toP1, thm:moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1}
+  By \ref{thm:exists_finite_toP1} there is a finite morphism \(\pi : C \to \PP^1\) over
+  \(k\); apply \ref{thm:moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1}.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{remark}[The genus is the dimension of a finite-dimensional space]
+  \label{rem:genus_finite}
+  \uses{def:genus, thm:moduleFinite_hModule_one}
+  \leanok
+  For a smooth curve \(C\) over \(k\), the genus of Definition~\ref{def:genus} is the
+  \(k\)-dimension of \(H^1(C, \struct C)\), which by
+  \ref{thm:moduleFinite_hModule_one} is a finite-dimensional \(k\)-vector space; the
+  genus is therefore a well-defined natural number, attained as the cardinality of any
+  basis.
+\end{remark}

module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Category.Grp.Limits
public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.Mon
public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Grp

/-!
# Yoneda embedding of `Grp C`

We show that group objects are exactly those whose yoneda presheaf is a presheaf of groups,
by constructing the yoneda embedding `Grp C ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{v}` and
showing that it is fully faithful and its (essential) image is the representable functors.
-/

@[expose] public section

assert_not_exists Field

open CategoryTheory MonoidalCategory Limits Opposite CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj

namespace CategoryTheory
universe w v u
variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [CartesianMonoidalCategory C]
  {M G H X Y : C} [MonObj M] [GrpObj G] [GrpObj H]

variable (X) in
/-- If `X` represents a presheaf of monoids, then `X` is a monoid object. -/
@[to_additive (attr := implicit_reducible)
/-- If `X` represents a presheaf of additive monoids, then `X` is an additive monoid object. -/]
def GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{w}) (α : (F ⋙ forget _).RepresentableBy X) :
    GrpObj X where
  __ := MonObj.ofRepresentableBy X (F ⋙ forget₂ GrpCat MonCat) α
  inv := α.homEquiv'.symm (α.homEquiv (𝟙 _))⁻¹
  left_inv := by
    change lift (α.homEquiv'.symm (α.homEquiv (𝟙 X))⁻¹) (𝟙 X) ≫
      α.homEquiv'.symm (α.homEquiv' (fst X X) * α.homEquiv' (snd X X)) =
        toUnit X ≫ α.homEquiv'.symm 1
    apply α.homEquiv'.injective
    simp only [α.homEquiv'_comp, Equiv.apply_symm_apply, map_mul, map_one]
    simp only [← α.homEquiv'_comp, lift_fst, Equiv.apply_symm_apply, lift_snd]
    exact inv_mul_cancel (α.homEquiv (𝟙 X))
  right_inv := by
    change lift (𝟙 X) (α.homEquiv'.symm (α.homEquiv' (𝟙 X))⁻¹) ≫
      α.homEquiv'.symm (α.homEquiv' (fst X X) * α.homEquiv' (snd X X)) =
        toUnit X ≫ α.homEquiv'.symm 1
    apply α.homEquiv'.injective
    simp only [α.homEquiv'_comp, Equiv.apply_symm_apply, map_mul, map_one]
    simp only [← α.homEquiv'_comp]
    simp

/-- If `G` is a group object, then `Hom(X, G)` has a group structure. -/
@[to_additive
/-- If `G` is an additive group object, then `Hom(X, G)` has an additive group structure. -/]
abbrev Hom.group : Group (X ⟶ G) where
  inv f := f ≫ ι
  inv_mul_cancel f := calc
    lift (f ≫ ι) f ≫ μ
    _ = (f ≫ lift ι (𝟙 G)) ≫ μ := by simp
    _ = toUnit X ≫ η := by rw [Category.assoc]; simp

scoped[CategoryTheory.MonObj] attribute [instance] Hom.group
scoped[CategoryTheory.AddMonObj] attribute [instance] Hom.addGroup

@[to_additive]
lemma Hom.inv_def (f : X ⟶ G) : f⁻¹ = f ≫ ι := rfl

variable (G) in
/-- If `G` is a group object, then `Hom(-, G)` is a presheaf of groups. -/
@[to_additive (attr := simps)
/-- If `G` is an additive group object, then `Hom(-, G)` is a presheaf of additive groups. -/]
def yonedaGrpObj : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{v} where
  obj X := GrpCat.of (unop X ⟶ G)
  map φ := GrpCat.ofHom ((yonedaMonObj G).map φ).hom

variable (G) in

   121	  rw [Category.assoc, h4] at h5
   122	  simp only [Category.assoc, Iso.inv_hom_id, Category.comp_id] at h5
   123	  exact h5
   124	
   125	/-- `g^d/f^e = Xⱼ/Xᵢ`: the mathlib localization element of the pair `(Xᵢ, Xⱼ)` is the chart
   126	coordinate (generalizing `P1.isLocalizationElem_eq` to both charts). -/
   127	theorem isLocalizationElem_X_eq (i j : Fin 2) :
   128	    Away.isLocalizationElem (X_mem k i) (X_mem k j) = chartCoord k i j := by
   129	  rw [Away.isLocalizationElem, chartCoord_eq]
   130	  congr 1
   131	  exact pow_one _
   132	
   133	/-- **The chart coordinate cuts out the overlap**: on `ℙ¹`, the scheme-level basic open of
   134	the section `t = Xⱼ/Xᵢ ∈ Γ(D₊(Xᵢ))` is the chart overlap `D₊(Xᵢ) ⊓ D₊(Xⱼ)`. -/
   135	theorem basicOpen_awayToSection_chartCoord (i j : Fin 2) :
   136	    (P1 k).basicOpen ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X i)).hom (chartCoord k i j)) =
   137	      chartOpen k i ⊓ chartOpen k j := by
   138	  change (Proj 𝒜).basicOpen ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X i)).hom (chartCoord k i j)) =
   139	    Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X i) ⊓ Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X j)
   140	  have hpre : (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X i)).ι ⁻¹ᵁ
   141	        ((Proj 𝒜).basicOpen ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X i)).hom (chartCoord k i j))) =
   142	      (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X i)).ι ⁻¹ᵁ Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X j) := by
   143	    rw [← Scheme.Opens.toSpecΓ_preimage_basicOpen]
   144	    conv_rhs => rw [basicOpen_ι_eq k (X_mem k i) one_pos]
   145	    change _ = Proj.basicOpenToSpec 𝒜 (X i) ⁻¹ᵁ
   146	      (Proj.awayι 𝒜 (X i) (X_mem k i) one_pos ⁻¹ᵁ Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X j))
   147	    rw [Proj.awayι_preimage_basicOpen 𝒜 (X_mem k i) one_pos (X_mem k j) one_pos,
   148	      isLocalizationElem_X_eq k i j]
   149	    rfl
   150	  have himg := congrArg (fun W => (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X i)).ι ''ᵁ W) hpre
   151	  simp only [Scheme.Hom.image_preimage_eq_opensRange_inf, Scheme.Opens.opensRange_ι]
   152	    at himg
   153	  have hle : (Proj 𝒜).basicOpen ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X i)).hom (chartCoord k i j)) ≤
   154	      Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X i) := (Proj 𝒜).basicOpen_le _
   155	  calc (Proj 𝒜).basicOpen ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X i)).hom (chartCoord k i j))
   156	      = Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X i) ⊓
   157	          (Proj 𝒜).basicOpen ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X i)).hom (chartCoord k i j)) :=
   158	        (inf_eq_right.mpr hle).symm
   159	    _ = Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X i) ⊓ Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X j) := himg
   160	
   161	/-! ### The Laurent generators as restrictions from the charts -/
   162	
   163	/-- Under the overlap identification, `T` is the restriction to the overlap of the chart-0
   164	coordinate `X₁/X₀ ∈ Γ(D₊(X₀))`. -/
   165	theorem overlapSectionsEquiv_symm_T :
   166	    (overlapSectionsEquiv k).symm (LaurentPolynomial.T 1) =
   167	      ((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE (overlap_le_left k)).op).hom
   168	        ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0)).hom (chartCoord k 0 1)) := by
   169	  apply (overlapSectionsEquiv k).injective
   170	  rw [RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply, res_awayToSection_left, overlapSectionsEquiv_awayToSection,
   171	    overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapLeft, awayAlgEquiv_chartCoord k fin_zero_ne_one,
   172	    Polynomial.toLaurent_X]
   173	
   174	/-- Under the overlap identification, `T⁻¹` is the restriction to the overlap of the
   175	chart-1 coordinate `X₀/X₁ ∈ Γ(D₊(X₁))`. -/
   176	theorem overlapSectionsEquiv_symm_T_neg :
   177	    (overlapSectionsEquiv k).symm (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1)) =
   178	      ((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE (overlap_le_right k)).op).hom
   179	        ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 1)).hom (chartCoord k 1 0)) := by
   180	  apply (overlapSectionsEquiv k).injective
   181	  rw [RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply, res_awayToSection_right, overlapSectionsEquiv_awayToSection,
   182	    overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapRight_chartCoord]
   183	
   184	/-- The overlap identification matches the algebra map of the homogeneous localization
   185	with that of the Laurent polynomial ring. -/
   186	theorem overlapSectionsEquiv_symm_algebraMap (r : k) :
   187	    (overlapSectionsEquiv k).symm (algebraMap k (LaurentPolynomial k) r) =
   188	      (Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)).hom (algebraMap k (Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) r) := by
   189	  apply (overlapSectionsEquiv k).injective
   190	  rw [RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply, overlapSectionsEquiv_awayToSection]
   191	  exact ((overlapAlgEquiv k).commutes r).symm

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.AffineVanishing
7	
8	/-!
9	# The two-affine-cover H¹ cokernel bridge
10	
11	For a scheme `X` over `Spec k` covered by two affine opens `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`, this file
12	computes the degree-one cohomology of the structure sheaf (as a sheaf of `k`-modules on
13	the small Zariski site, `Sheaf.HModule`) as an explicit cokernel of a map of section
14	modules:
15	
16	`H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪ₖ) ≃ₗ[k] Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range((s₀, s₁) ↦ s₀|_{U₀⊓U₁} - s₁|_{U₀⊓U₁})`
17	
18	(`AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.h1CokEquiv`, with the cokernel carrier
19	`AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.H1Cok`). This is the computational access point for the genus
20	of a curve: `genus C = finrank k H¹ₖ(C, 𝒪_C)` becomes the corank of an explicit map of
21	function spaces.
22	
23	**Hypotheses actually used**: `X` any scheme over `Spec k`, `IsAffineOpen U₀`,
24	`IsAffineOpen U₁`, `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`. In particular *no* affineness (or even
25	quasi-compactness) hypothesis on the intersection `U₀ ⊓ U₁` is needed — unlike for the
26	classical Čech-complex identification, the derived-functor Mayer–Vietoris sequence of
27	`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.MayerVietoris` is exact regardless, and affineness of the
28	two pieces alone kills their `H¹'` (`IsAffineOpen.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one`).
29	
30	## Main declarations
31	
32	* `Scheme.twoCoverSquare` — the Mayer–Vietoris square `(U₀ ⊓ U₁, U₀, U₁, ⊤)` on the
33	  small Zariski site of `X`, for a covering pair of opens.
34	* `Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv` — the general-coefficients form: for any sheaf `F` of
35	  `k`-modules with `H¹'(U₀, F)` and `H¹'(U₁, F)` subsingletons,
36	  `HModule F 1 ≃ₗ[k] F(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range(moduleDiff)` (reusable for twisted sheaves).
37	* `TwoCover.diff k X U₀ U₁` — the difference map `Γ(U₀) × Γ(U₁) →ₗ[k] Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)`.
38	* `TwoCover.H1Cok k X U₀ U₁` — the cokernel carrier `Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range diff`.
39	* `TwoCover.delta` — the connecting map `Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) →ₗ[k] HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1`
40	  ("class of a section on the overlap").
41	* `TwoCover.h1CokEquiv : HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1 ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok k X U₀ U₁`.
42	* Compatibility: `h1CokEquiv_delta` (`h1CokEquiv ∘ delta = Quotient.mk`),
43	  `delta_surjective`, `delta_diff`, `delta_resHom_left/right` and
44	  `h1Cok_mk_resHom_left/right` (classes of sections extending to `U₀` or `U₁` vanish).
45	
46	The `k`-module structure on `Γ(X, U)` is `Scheme.overModule` (restriction of scalars
47	along the structure morphism), activated as a local instance as in
48	`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.ModuleKSheaf`.
49	-/
50	
51	set_option autoImplicit false
52	
53	universe u
54	
55	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace
56	
57	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
58	
59	open CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology
60	
61	section Square
62	
63	variable (X : Scheme.{u}) (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
64	
65	/-- The Mayer–Vietoris square `(U₀ ⊓ U₁, U₀, U₁, ⊤)` on the small Zariski site of a
66	scheme `X`, for two opens covering `X`. -/
67	noncomputable def Scheme.twoCoverSquare (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) :
68	    (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X : TopCat)).MayerVietorisSquare :=
69	  Opens.mayerVietorisSquare'
70	    { X₁ := U₀ ⊓ U₁
71	      X₂ := U₀
72	      X₃ := U₁
73	      X₄ := ⊤
74	      f₁₂ := homOfLE inf_le_left
75	      f₁₃ := homOfLE inf_le_right
76	      f₂₄ := homOfLE le_top
77	      f₃₄ := homOfLE le_top
78	      fac := Subsingleton.elim _ _ } hcov.symm rfl
79	
80	end Square
81	
82	section GeneralCoefficients
83	
84	variable (k : Type u) [CommRing k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
85	variable (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
86	
87	/-- **The two-cover H¹ computation, general coefficients.** For a sheaf `F` of
88	`k`-modules on the small Zariski site of `X`, two opens with `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤` and
89	vanishing `H¹'(U₀, F)`, `H¹'(U₁, F)`, the degree-one cohomology of the site is the
90	cokernel of the restriction-difference map `F(U₀) × F(U₁) → F(U₀ ⊓ U₁)`. -/
91	noncomputable def Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv
92	    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X : TopCat)) (ModuleCat.{u} k))
93	    (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)
94	    [Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' F U₀ 1)] [Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' F U₁ 1)] :
95	    Sheaf.HModule F 1 ≃ₗ[k]
96	      (F.obj.obj (op (U₀ ⊓ U₁)) ⧸
97	        LinearMap.range ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDiff F)) :=
98	  letI : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' F (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₂ 1) :=
99	    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' F U₀ 1))
100	  letI : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' F (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₃ 1) :=
101	    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' F U₁ 1))
102	  (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens)) F 1).trans
103	    ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv F).symm
104	
105	end GeneralCoefficients
106	
107	namespace TwoCover
108	
109	variable (k : Type u) [CommRing k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
110	variable (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
111	
112	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule
113	
114	/-- The restriction-difference map `Γ(X, U₀) × Γ(X, U₁) →ₗ[k] Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)`,
115	`(s₀, s₁) ↦ s₀|_{U₀ ⊓ U₁} - s₁|_{U₀ ⊓ U₁}` (see `TwoCover.diff_apply`), with the
116	`k`-module structures of `Scheme.overModule`. -/
117	noncomputable def diff : (Γ(X, U₀) × Γ(X, U₁)) →ₗ[k] Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) :=
118	  ((X.moduleKSheaf k).obj.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀)).op).hom.comp
119	      (LinearMap.fst k _ _) -
120	    ((X.moduleKSheaf k).obj.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)).op).hom.comp
121	      (LinearMap.snd k _ _)
122	
123	lemma diff_apply (t : Γ(X, U₀) × Γ(X, U₁)) :
124	    diff k X U₀ U₁ t = X.resHom inf_le_left t.1 - X.resHom inf_le_right t.2 :=
125	  rfl
126	
127	/-- The two-cover difference map is the Mayer–Vietoris restriction-difference map of the
128	associated square. -/
129	lemma diff_eq_moduleDiff (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) :
130	    diff k X U₀ U₁ = (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDiff (X.moduleKSheaf k) :=
131	  rfl
132	
133	/-- **The two-cover H¹ cokernel carrier**: the cokernel of the restriction-difference
134	map, `Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range (TwoCover.diff)`. For `U₀, U₁` an affine open cover this is
135	`H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪)` (see `TwoCover.h1CokEquiv`); it is a plain quotient of section modules, so
136	`Module.finrank` arguments can be run on it directly. -/
137	noncomputable abbrev H1Cok : Type u :=
138	  Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ LinearMap.range (diff k X U₀ U₁)
139	
140	/-- A section extending to `U₀` has vanishing class in `H1Cok`. -/
141	lemma h1Cok_mk_resHom_left (t : Γ(X, U₀)) :
142	    (Submodule.Quotient.mk (X.resHom inf_le_left t) : H1Cok k X U₀ U₁) = 0 := by
143	  rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
144	  exact ⟨(t, 0), by rw [diff_apply]; simp⟩
145	
146	/-- A section extending to `U₁` has vanishing class in `H1Cok`. -/
147	lemma h1Cok_mk_resHom_right (t : Γ(X, U₁)) :
148	    (Submodule.Quotient.mk (X.resHom inf_le_right t) : H1Cok k X U₀ U₁) = 0 := by
149	  rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
150	  refine ⟨(0, -t), ?_⟩
151	  rw [diff_apply]
152	  simp
153	
154	section Bridge
155	
156	variable (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)
157	
158	/-- The two-cover connecting map: the degree-one cohomology class of a section on the
159	overlap `U₀ ⊓ U₁`, in the cohomology `Sheaf.HModule` of the small Zariski site of `X`. -/
160	noncomputable def delta :
161	    Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) →ₗ[k] Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1 :=
162	  ((Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens))
163	      (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1).symm.toLinearMap).comp
164	    ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta (X.moduleKSheaf k))
165	
166	/-- The connecting class of a difference of restrictions vanishes. -/
167	lemma delta_diff (t : Γ(X, U₀) × Γ(X, U₁)) :
168	    delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov (diff k X U₀ U₁ t) = 0 := by
169	  have h : (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta (X.moduleKSheaf k)
170	      (diff k X U₀ U₁ t) = 0 :=
171	    (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta_moduleDiff (X.moduleKSheaf k) t
172	  rw [show delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov (diff k X U₀ U₁ t) =
173	      (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens))
174	          (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1).symm
175	        ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta (X.moduleKSheaf k)
176	          (diff k X U₀ U₁ t)) from rfl, h]
177	  exact map_zero _
178	
179	/-- The connecting class of a section extending to `U₀` vanishes. -/
180	lemma delta_resHom_left (t : Γ(X, U₀)) :
181	    delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov (X.resHom inf_le_left t) = 0 := by
182	  have h : X.resHom inf_le_left t = diff k X U₀ U₁ (t, 0) := by
183	    rw [diff_apply]
184	    simp
185	  rw [h, delta_diff]
186	
187	/-- The connecting class of a section extending to `U₁` vanishes. -/
188	lemma delta_resHom_right (t : Γ(X, U₁)) :
189	    delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov (X.resHom inf_le_right t) = 0 := by
190	  have h : X.resHom inf_le_right t = -diff k X U₀ U₁ (0, t) := by
191	    rw [diff_apply]
192	    simp
193	  rw [h, map_neg, delta_diff, neg_zero]
194	
195	variable (hU₀ : IsAffineOpen U₀) (hU₁ : IsAffineOpen U₁)
196	
197	include hU₀ hU₁ in
198	/-- For an affine two-cover, the connecting map is surjective: every degree-one class
199	comes from a section on the overlap. -/
200	lemma delta_surjective : Function.Surjective (delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov) := by
201	  haveI : Subsingleton
202	      (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₂ 1) :=
203	    hU₀.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one k
204	  haveI : Subsingleton
205	      (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₃ 1) :=
206	    hU₁.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one k
207	  intro y
208	  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta_surjective (X.moduleKSheaf k)
209	    ((Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens))
210	      (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1) y)
211	  refine ⟨s, ?_⟩
212	  rw [show delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s =
213	      (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens))
214	          (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1).symm
215	        ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta (X.moduleKSheaf k) s) from rfl, hs,
216	    LinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply]
217	
218	/-- **The two-affine-cover H¹ cokernel bridge.** For a scheme `X` over `Spec k` and two
219	affine opens with `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`, the degree-one cohomology of the structure sheaf as a
220	sheaf of `k`-modules on the small Zariski site of `X` is the cokernel of the
221	restriction-difference map on sections:
222	`H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪) ≃ₗ[k] Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range((s₀, s₁) ↦ s₀|∩ - s₁|∩)`.
223	The inverse sends the class of a section on the overlap to its connecting class
224	(`TwoCover.h1CokEquiv_delta`). -/
225	noncomputable def h1CokEquiv :
226	    Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1 ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok k X U₀ U₁ :=
227	  letI : Subsingleton
228	      (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₂ 1) :=
229	    hU₀.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one k
230	  letI : Subsingleton
231	      (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₃ 1) :=
232	    hU₁.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one k
233	  (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens))
234	      (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1).trans
235	    ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv (X.moduleKSheaf k)).symm
236	
237	/-- Compatibility of the bridge with the connecting map: the bridge sends the connecting
238	class of a section on the overlap to its class in the cokernel. -/
239	lemma h1CokEquiv_delta (s : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
240	    h1CokEquiv k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁ (delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s) =
241	      Submodule.Quotient.mk s := by
242	  haveI : Subsingleton
243	      (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₂ 1) :=
244	    hU₀.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one k
245	  haveI : Subsingleton
246	      (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₃ 1) :=
247	    hU₁.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one k
248	  apply ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv (X.moduleKSheaf k)).injective
249	  calc ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv (X.moduleKSheaf k))
250	        (h1CokEquiv k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁ (delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s))
251	      = ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv (X.moduleKSheaf k))
252	          (((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv (X.moduleKSheaf k)).symm
253	            ((Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule'
254	                (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens)) (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1)
255	              ((Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule'
256	                  (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens)) (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1).symm
257	                ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta (X.moduleKSheaf k) s)))) :=
258	        rfl
259	    _ = (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta (X.moduleKSheaf k) s := by
260	        rw [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
261	    _ = ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv (X.moduleKSheaf k))
262	          (Submodule.Quotient.mk s) :=
263	        (MayerVietorisSquare.h1LinearEquiv_mk (S := X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov)
264	          (X.moduleKSheaf k) s).symm

11	/-!
12	# A finite morphism from the curve to the projective line
13	
14	For the smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curve `C` over `k`, this file is about the
15	existence and the basic consequences of a **finite** `k`-morphism `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹`.
16	
17	## Contents
18	
19	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.of_locallyQuasiFinite_of_comp` — the general Zariski-main-theorem
20	  reduction: a locally quasi-finite morphism which is proper over a separated base is finite.
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite` — the specialization: a locally
22	  quasi-finite `k`-morphism from the proper curve `C` to `ℙ¹` is finite.
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite` — the same, in existential
24	  form: to produce a finite `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` over `k` it suffices to produce a locally
25	  quasi-finite one.
26	* Preimage bookkeeping for a finite `π`, consumed by the two-lattice finiteness argument for
27	  `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)`: the preimages of the two standard charts are affine opens covering `C`
28	  (`isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen`, `preimage_chartOpen_sup`), and the section ring of each
29	  preimage is module-finite over the section ring of the chart (`finite_app_chartOpen`).
30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_toP1` — the **existence** of a finite `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` over
31	  `k`, by spreading out a transcendental rational function
32	  (`AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.RationalToP1`) and applying the reduction above; see its
33	  docstring for the proof route.
34	-/
35	
36	set_option autoImplicit false
37	
38	universe u
39	
40	open CategoryTheory MvPolynomial
41	
42	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
43	
44	/-- **Zariski's main theorem, cancellation form**: a locally quasi-finite morphism `π` such
45	that `π ≫ g` is proper and `g` is separated is finite. (Properness of `π` follows by
46	cancellation, and a proper locally quasi-finite morphism is finite.) -/
47	theorem IsFinite.of_locallyQuasiFinite_of_comp {X Y S : Scheme.{u}}
48	    (π : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S) [LocallyQuasiFinite π] [IsSeparated g] [IsProper (π ≫ g)] :
49	    IsFinite π :=
50	  have : IsProper π := IsProper.of_comp π g
51	  IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite π
52	
53	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
54	
55	section ZMT
56	
57	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
58	
59	/-- A locally quasi-finite `k`-morphism from a scheme which is proper over `k` to the
60	projective line is finite. This is the Zariski-main-theorem half of the construction of the
61	finite map `C ⟶ ℙ¹`: it reduces finiteness to local quasi-finiteness. -/
62	theorem isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f]
63	    (π : X ⟶ P1 k) [LocallyQuasiFinite π] (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = f) :
64	    IsFinite π :=
65	  have : IsProper (π ≫ P1.structureMap k) := hπ ▸ inferInstance
66	  IsFinite.of_locallyQuasiFinite_of_comp π (P1.structureMap k)
67	
68	end ZMT
69	
70	/-- To produce a finite `k`-morphism `C ⟶ ℙ¹` it suffices to produce a locally quasi-finite
71	one; Zariski's main theorem upgrades it. -/
72	theorem exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
73	    (h : ∃ π : C.left ⟶ P1 k, LocallyQuasiFinite π ∧ π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) :
74	    ∃ π : C.left ⟶ P1 k, IsFinite π ∧ π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom := by
75	  obtain ⟨π, hqf, hcomp⟩ := h
76	  exact ⟨π, isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite C.hom π hcomp, hcomp⟩
77	
78	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
79	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
80	
81	/-- **Existence of a finite map to the projective line**: on the smooth, proper,
82	geometrically irreducible curve `C/k` there is a finite `k`-morphism `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹`.
83	
84	This is the keystone the two-lattice finiteness argument for `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` consumes.
85	
86	Proof route (see `informal/route-decision.md`, Wave 1 item 4):
87	1. `C` is integral (smooth ⟹ geometrically reduced, `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.
88	   GeometricallyReduced`, plus geometric irreducibility, `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.Basic`),
89	   and the function field of `C` contains an element transcendental over `k`: the étale
90	   coordinate of a standard smooth chart of relative dimension `1`
91	   (`SmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_transcendental_functionField`, via the structure
92	   theorem for standard smooth algebras of Stacks 00T7);
93	2. the transcendental function spreads out to a morphism `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` over `k`: the stalks
94	   of `C` are valuation rings (localizations of the Dedekind chart rings,
95	   `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.DedekindSections` and `Curve.StalksDVR`), so at each point
96	   either `f` or `1/f` is a regular germ; the two chart morphisms agree generically by the
97	   gluing identity `P1.fromSpecChart_units`, so the associated rational map `C ⤏ ℙ¹` is
98	   defined everywhere (`AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.RationalToP1`);
99	3. `π` maps the generic point to the generic point (transcendence again), hence has finite
100	   fibers on the height-one Noetherian space `C`, hence is locally quasi-finite;
101	4. conclude with `exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite` (Zariski's main theorem). -/
102	theorem exists_isFinite_toP1 :
103	    ∃ π : C.left ⟶ P1 k, IsFinite π ∧ π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom :=
104	  exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite (exists_locallyQuasiFinite_toP1 C.hom)
105	
106	/-! ### Preimage bookkeeping for a finite morphism to the projective line
107	
108	The next wave feeds these to the two-lattice/Mayer–Vietoris finiteness argument: the
109	preimages of the two standard charts form an affine cover of `C`, with section rings
110	module-finite over `k[t]`. Everything here only needs `π` finite (indeed mostly just
111	affine), not how it was constructed. -/
112	
113	section Preimages
114	
115	variable {Y : Scheme.{u}} (π : Y ⟶ P1 k)
116	
117	/-- The preimage of each standard chart of `ℙ¹` under an affine (e.g. finite) morphism is an
118	affine open. -/
119	theorem isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen [IsAffineHom π] (i : Fin 2) :
120	    IsAffineOpen (π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k i) :=
121	  (P1.isAffineOpen_chartOpen k i).preimage π
122	
123	/-- The preimages of the two standard charts of `ℙ¹` cover the source. -/
124	theorem preimage_chartOpen_sup :
125	    π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊔ π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1 = ⊤ := by
126	  refine le_antisymm le_top fun x _ => ?_
127	  have h : π.base x ∈ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊔ P1.chartOpen k 1 := by
128	    rw [P1.chartOpen_sup]
129	    trivial
130	  rw [TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_sup] at h ⊢
131	  exact h
132	
133	/-- For a finite morphism `π : X ⟶ ℙ¹`, the section ring of the preimage of a standard chart
134	is module-finite over the section ring of the chart (that is, over `k[t]`, via
135	`P1.chartSectionsEquiv₀`/`₁`). -/
136	theorem finite_app_chartOpen [IsFinite π] (i : Fin 2) :
137	    RingHom.Finite (π.app (P1.chartOpen k i)).hom :=
138	  π.finite_app _ (P1.isAffineOpen_chartOpen k i)
139	
140	/-- For a finite morphism `π : X ⟶ ℙ¹`, the section ring of the preimage of the chart
141	overlap is module-finite over the section ring of the overlap (that is, over the Laurent
142	polynomial ring, via `P1.overlapSectionsEquiv`). -/
143	theorem finite_app_overlap [IsFinite π] :
144	    RingHom.Finite (π.app (Proj.basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k)
145	      (X 0 * X 1))).hom :=
146	  π.finite_app _ (P1.isAffineOpen_overlap k)
147	
148	end Preimages
149	
150	end AlgebraicGeometry
